chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: Talented players stuck in big bands without solos
summary: They talk about a saxophonist in Kansas City who was stuck in a big band, and how many talents never get a chance to solo.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I guess you didn't -- when you were in Kansas City, Bart hadn't commenced --
No, he hadn't. He was with what band? I don't remember. Was it Kirk? Was that the band --
He was with Jay McShann, but that was later --
That was later. I think he was with --
I think he was with Harlan Lenoard

Yeah. But I think he must have been with Kirk you know. But he didn't like a band like that, you know. He was just -- I guess he was maybe one of those kind of guys I've been trying to tell you about being stuck in a band and never getting a chance to play nothing. And when they did get a chance the guys found out what kind of guy he was, you know.
That's all. And you know, there's so much talent getting in these big bands that don't get a chance. They don't get a chance to play. Just stay up there and play that -- what the music is.

Of course they're getting a little experience really. But some guys they get a lot of experience and really nothing happens. You know. They have to get an outside job. That's what so many guys have had to get outside jobs. So many. You know what I mean?
